question_text:
Rule: 'An applicant is granted an interview ONLY IF they pass the written examination and possess a bachelor's degree.'
Fact: Jose passed the written examination but does not possess a bachelor's degree.
Conclusion: Is Jose eligible for an interview?

options.text: Yes, because passing the written exam is sufficient.
No, because both conditions must be satisfied.
Yes, if he submits an extension request.
Cannot be determined from the rule.

hint_ladder.title: Unawain ang 'ONLY IF'
hint_ladder.text: Para itong striktong guard na may checklist. Lahat ng item sa listahan ay dapat may check—walang puwedeng kulang. Recall: 'X ONLY IF Y' means Y is ...

hint_ladder.title: Double requirement ito
hint_ladder.text: Hindi 'OR' kundi 'AND' ang nasa rule. Kailangan both pumasa sa exam at may degree. Parang pagkuha ng police clearance: need both valid ID at barang...

hint_ladder.title: I-check si Jose
hint_ladder.text: May isa siyang na-meet (exam) pero kulang ng degree. Dahil 'ONLY IF' ay non-negotiable, kahit isang kulang, hindi pa rin pasok. Walang partial cred...

hint_ladder.title: Dalawang kandado, isang susi
hint_ladder.text: Visualize: pinto na may dalawang lock. May susi ka lang ng isa—hindi mo mabubuksan. Ganun din ang interview: need both keys. Kaya sagot ay hindi si...

A.text: You might have chosen A because your brain saw 'passed the exam' and jumped to a yes—akala mo sapat na, pero 'ONLY IF' requires both.

B.text: Correct. Both conditions are strictly necessary; kulang siya ng degree so the interview is impossible—parang kulang ng pirma sa form.

C.text: You might have chosen C because you wish there was a loophole, but the rule doesn’t mention extensions—nag-iimbento ka lang ng extra step.

D.text: You might have chosen D because parang kulang ang info, pero the rule is crystal clear—mabilisang konklusyon na walang sapat na basehan.

next_time_rule: Sa 'ONLY IF,' isipin mo dalawang susi sa isang lock—kailangan parehas, o walang mangyayari. Both conditions = mandatory.
blueprint_id: Logical Reasoning — Necessary vs Sufficient Conditions
deconstruct_text:
Tara, gawin nating Pinoy ang logic. Kunwari nag-a-apply ka ng DOST scholarship, at rule: 'Scholar ka ONLY IF pumasa sa exam at may average na 90.' Kahit perfect sa exam, kung 89 lang average, ligwak. Same rule dito: interview ONLY IF both pumasa at degree holder.

Si Jose, pasado sa exam pero walang degree. Parang nag-apply sa trabaho sa LGU na required ang Civil Service eligibility—kahit may experience ka, kung wala ang eligibility, hindi ka iha-hire. Kaya kahit may isa, kulang pa rin.

Mental trick: Baligtarin mo—'If na-interview, then pumasa at may degree.' Kung may interview si Jose, dapat both true; pero hindi true ang degree. Kaya walang interview. Basta 'ONLY IF,' mandatory lahat ng kasunod.
